movement_source: row 'Cash return on equity', column Year to Sep 24 -> column Year to Sep 25
headline: NAB's Cash ROE fell 20 bps, from 11.6% in FY24 to 11.4% in FY25 (ev-1, ev-5, ev-13). The decline is almost entirely a denominator story: cash earnings were essentially flat at $7,091m versus $7,102m, down $11m or 0.2% (ev-2, ev-8, ev-17, ev-18), while total average equity attributable to owners rose $1,316m from $61,039m to $62,355m (ev-3). NAB itself frames FY25 earnings as "broadly stable compared with FY24 including higher credit impairment charges", with cash EPS up 1% (ev-15) — EPS outpaced ROE because the share count fell from 3,074m to 3,063m after the on-market buy-back (ev-19, ev-20). On the statutory basis the fall was materially larger: statutory ROE dropped 60 bps from 11.4% to 10.8% (ev-4, ev-6), as statutory profit fell $201m or 2.9% (ev-8, ev-18) — a definitional difference driven by non-cash earnings items. NAB publishes no ROE walk chart; the earnings/equity split below is derived arithmetically.

drivers.bank_label: Total average equity (attributable to owners of the Company)
drivers.columns: Year to Sep 25 less Year to Sep 24
drivers.narrative: Derived, not disclosed: total delta (-0.20ppt) less earnings effect. Average equity attributable to owners rose $1,316m, $61,039m to $62,355m (+2.2%); average equity $61,433m to $63,106m, with average non-controlling interests widening $394m to $751m. NAB cites retention plus "increased long term investment in the business, and completion of the on-market share buy-back" (16,572k shares vs 60,690k in FY24), so buybacks slowed sharply and no longer offset retained earnings.

drivers.columns: Year to Sep 25 less Year to Sep 24
drivers.narrative: Derived, not disclosed: FY24 ROE 11.6% x cash earnings growth of -0.2% (-$11m, $7,102m to $7,091m) at constant equity. NAB attributes the flat result to net interest income +$644m or 3.8%, offset by operating expenses +$435m or 4.6%, credit impairment charge +$105m or 14.4% "driven by a higher level of individually assessed credit impairment charge primarily in Corporate and Institutional Banking", and other operating income -$67m or 1.9%.

notable_items: Credit impairment charge increased $105m or 14.4%, following a write-back position in FY24 (ev-11, ev-15)
Operating expenses include an increase of $130m for payroll review and remediation costs within the total $435m rise (ev-10)
Completion of the on-market share buy-back contributed to the 65 bps FY25 fall in the CET1 ratio to 11.70% (ev-16)

disagreements.topic: Cash vs statutory ROE movement FY25 v FY24
disagreements.explanation: Cash ROE is NAB's headline measure and excludes non-cash earnings items; statutory ROE uses net profit attributable to owners, which fell $201m or 2.9% versus a $11m or 0.2% fall in cash earnings, over the same average equity base, producing a three-times-larger ROE decline.

limitations: NAB publishes no ROE walk or bridge chart for FY25 v FY24 in either document, so both contributions are arithmetic derivations from the ROE endpoints and the disclosed cash earnings movement, not bank-disclosed bars. Confidence is capped accordingly.

The equity_effect of -0.18ppt is a residual (total delta less earnings effect) and therefore absorbs the interaction term; NAB does not separately quantify retained earnings, buyback or DRP contributions to AVERAGE equity.

The CET1 movement charts in both documents (results book p.30, presentation p.29) cover Mar 25 to Sep 25 — a half-on-half comparison, not the FY25 v FY24 task span — so none of their bars is used as a contribution. They are regulatory capital ratio walks, not equity-dollar walks, in any case.
The average non-controlling interests line nearly doubled ($394m to $751m), which reduces the ROE denominator; NAB does not explain this movement on the ROE note page.
NAB's own narrative on p.6 of the results book characterises cash earnings as 'broadly stable', a qualification that means the earnings effect is genuinely near zero rather than a meaningful driver.
